question: Europa Clipper is the first mission designed to conduct a detailed study of _________'s moon Europa.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jupiter**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Europa Clipper** is a mission developed by **NASA** to study Jupiter’s icy moon, **Europa**, in detail.
 
• The mission is specifically aimed at investigating Europa’s **subsurface ocean** and assessing its potential habitability for life.
 
• Europa is one of Jupiter’s **Galilean moons**, discovered by Galileo Galilei in 1610, and is considered one of the most promising places in our solar system for extraterrestrial life due to its subsurface ocean.
 
• The Europa Clipper spacecraft will carry a suite of **scientific instruments** designed to study Europa’s surface, atmosphere, and internal composition, including its **ice crust and liquid water ocean**.
 
• The mission is expected to be launched in the **mid-2020s** using NASA’s **Space Launch System (SLS)** or another commercial rocket.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Europa’s Characteristics:**

 
 
• Europa is the **sixth-largest moon** in the solar system and the fourth-largest of Jupiter’s 79 known moons.
 
• Its surface is composed mainly of **water ice**, and it is believed to have a **subsurface ocean** beneath its icy crust.
 
• The moon has a relatively young surface, marked by **cracks and ridges** but very few craters, indicating active geological processes.
 
 
 
• **Europa Clipper’s Scientific Goals:**
 
 
• Investigate the thickness of Europa’s **ice shell** and the depth and salinity of its subsurface ocean.
 
• Examine the moon’s **surface composition** to identify organic compounds and other materials that could support life.
 
• Study the **geology** of the moon, including surface features like ridges and cracks, to understand its tectonic activity.
 
• Analyze Europa’s **thin atmosphere**, primarily composed of oxygen, to understand its interactions with Jupiter’s magnetosphere.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Studying Europa:**
 
 
• Europa’s subsurface ocean may contain more than **twice the amount of water** found on Earth, making it a prime candidate in the search for extraterrestrial life.
 
• The moon’s geological activity, combined with the potential presence of **organic molecules**, creates an environment that could support microbial life.
 
• Understanding Europa could provide insights into the habitability of icy worlds beyond Earth.
 
 
 
• **Other Missions to Jupiter:**
 
 
• **Galileo Mission:** NASA’s spacecraft orbited Jupiter from 1995 to 2003, providing the first evidence of Europa’s subsurface ocean.
 
• **Juno Mission:** Launched in 2011, Juno is currently studying Jupiter’s atmosphere, magnetic field, and auroras.
 
• **JUICE (Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer):** A mission by the European Space Agency (ESA) set to launch in 2023 to study Europa, Ganymede, and Callisto.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Europa’s Subsurface Ocean:** Europa’s ocean is estimated to be **60-150 kilometers deep** and is kept liquid due to heat generated by tidal forces from Jupiter’s gravity.
 
• **Radiation Exposure:** Europa’s surface is exposed to intense radiation from Jupiter’s magnetosphere, which might affect the survival of any potential surface organisms.
 
• **Plume Activity:** Observations from the Hubble Space Telescope suggest the presence of **water vapor plumes** erupting from Europa’s surface, which could provide direct access to the subsurface ocean for analysis.
 
• **Scientific Collaboration:** The Europa Clipper mission involves collaboration between multiple NASA centers and international partners, ensuring a comprehensive study of the moon.
